correctness.rationale: The corona block over one size-s nilpotent base block has characteristic polynomial (z+1)^(2s) and one-dimensional 1-eigenspace, giving one size-2s block. Lifting that block to the wave gives characteristic polynomial (z²+z+1)^(2s) and a one-dimensional eigenspace for each primitive cube root, hence two size-2s blocks over the splitting field. Their unipotent orders are the least powers of two at least 2s. Raising to a power divisible by three gives each block nullity min(2s,2^v2(k)): after extracting the 2-part the odd exponent gives an invertible cofactor of the linear term. Otherwise neither eigenvalue can give a fixed vector. Rank is invariant under field extension. The kernel dimensions strictly increase at the dyadic thresholds up to saturation, and subtraction gives the claimed POPULATIONS of states, not numbers of cycles. For the converse, T+T^−1=diag(A,A) excludes wave eigenvalue 1 since A is invertible, so if the odd part is three then all A eigenvalues equal 1. A+A^−1=diag(B,B) then forces nilpotence. The tree determinant is the parity matching polynomial; Lucas parity and the endpoint recurrence give the single path block, and the odd-coordinate cube layer squares to I, giving exactly n/2 size-two base blocks. The displayed family counts follow from the same nullities, including saturation at the last path threshold.
residual_risks: Replay covers only three small binary examples; arbitrary graphs, finite extension fields and the infinite families are justified algebraically, not by finite replay. The checker stdout label 'cycles' denotes state populations in the code, consistent with the Finding.
